---
title: "Measure estimated stem levels"
subtitle: "Native-time vocals, drums, bass and other source levels with explicit provenance."
sidebar: cookbook
---

`audio.stem_levels` summarizes four estimated HTDemucs source waveforms. It returns
`default` and `diagnostics` series on the input audio clock. The default columns
are `vocals`, `drums`, `bass`, and `other`; these are model source names, not verified
instrument annotations or source-presence probabilities.

## Extract levels

Install `natural-features[source_separation]`. This extra requires Demucs 4.0.1
and SciPy, independently of CREPE. Extraction uses the fixed upstream
`955717e8-8726e21a.th` checkpoint, verified against SHA256
`8726e21a993978c7ba086d3872e7608d7d5bfca646ca4aca459ffda844faa8b4`
before loading. `local_files_only=True` is the default; missing or altered assets
raise an error. Set it to false explicitly to download the pinned public asset.

```{python}
#| eval: false
from natural_features.features.audio import audio_stem_levels

# stim is an AudioStimulus containing scaled floating-point mono/stereo audio.
out = audio_stem_levels(
    stim,
    separator_checkpoint="/path/to/955717e8-8726e21a.th",
    hop_s=0.1,
    window_s=0.25,
    units="dbfs",       # or "rms" for linear amplitude
    db_floor=-120.0,
)
levels, diagnostics = out["default"], out["diagnostics"]
print(levels.coords["feature"], levels.times_s, levels.time_bounds_s)
```

The registry identifier is `audio.stem_levels`. The high-level planner requires
the normal optional-backend opt-in (`budget="allow_python"`). Recipe execution
preserves both named outputs.

## What is measured

Each complete, untapered window computes the square root of the mean squared
samples across time **and both channels**. Channels are not averaged before
measuring energy, so opposing-polarity stereo does not cancel. Windows use rounded
integer sample lengths and hops; exact bounds and realized rates are retained.
Partial end windows are omitted. Inputs shorter than one window produce empty
outputs after the normal strict backend checks.

`units="dbfs"` means `20*log10(RMS)` with unity sample amplitude as reference,
floored at `db_floor`. It is not LUFS or acoustic SPL. In linear RMS output, the
floor does not alter values. Per-stem `valid`, `silent`, and `below_floor`
diagnostics distinguish numerical validity, exact zero energy, and a clipped dB
representation. Quiet nonzero estimates remain distinguishable from silence.

The level path normalizes the whole stereo input by a common RMS, restores that
gain after separation, and removes each estimated channel's global DC. There is
no per-stem gain normalization. The existing vocal-F0 adapter retains its previous
normalization and mono-stem behavior. Source levels are independent of F0
acceptance: an unvoiced consonant can contribute vocal-stem energy.

`include_ratio=True` explicitly appends `vocals_to_accompaniment_db`. Accompaniment
is the **waveform sum** of drums, bass and other, followed by stereo RMS. The ratio
is NaN unless both vocal and accompaniment RMS are positive; `ratio_valid` reports
support. Its units remain dB even with `units="rms"`; per-column units are recorded.
This is not a probability or fraction of mixture energy. Summing stem energies
would drop cross terms and answer a different question.

## Context and validation limits

Although each level has a local observation window, separation and normalization
depend on the entire supplied recording. Metadata declares whole-input,
bidirectional dependencies, the model hash and runtime versions, resampling,
7.8-second model segments, overlap 0.25, and zero random shifts. Recordings cut
into different extraction contexts need not yield identical levels.

Leakage can have nonzero energy, and a weak source can be suppressed. These
diagnostics do not classify leakage or establish vocal activity. Known-stem tests
check the RMS, stereo, ratio and missingness arithmetic. An opt-in real-model
smoke test checks execution, timing, and common-gain behavior:

```bash
NF_TEST_VOCAL_F0_CHECKPOINT=/path/to/955717e8-8726e21a.th \
  pytest -q tests/external/test_stem_levels_external.py
```

Neither establishes separation accuracy on commercial recordings. Validate that
separately against reference sources appropriate to the intended domain. Study
windows, scanner alignment, nuisance controls and neural model selection remain
downstream choices.
